item.text: Historical evidence shows that caster survival can fail before the first leak, particularly when artillery splash injures the healer too. I’m testing structures that fund early interception while keeping the caster healed. The plan will explicitly account for civilian roadblock clearance and the later central armored enemies, rather than assuming that surviving the opening is enough.

item.text: I’ve selected a seven-ID structure with four lane interceptors, Steward for the aircraft, and Ansel supported by Spot’s local healing. The first candidate moves Spot’s healing into the first caster barrage. That is the key unverified handoff; the check and simulation will test whether the actual healing targets support it.

Two civilians remain neutral and require roadblock clearance plus absence of officer/artillery threats.

candidates.assessment: Fang and Vanilla finance four melee lanes and improve central damage. Persistent lower duelist requires medical geometry that competes with aircraft and upper-outer recovery; two-block final armor queues remain unverified.

Sniper/caster shared lanes reduce ground slots, but straight crossing contact is short against3500HP runners and3300HP officers. Unsupported splash and probabilistic talents cannot provide missing kills.

Cheap three-block opening permits four simultaneous lanes. Living duelist release funds a durable lower replacement; Spot heals Ansel during first barrage, freeing Ansel for Steward. Later upper/lower armor damage is geometrically separated.

Candidate 1 completed as a LOSS. The earliest break was the withdrawal handoff: it changed the artillery target to Ansel, and splash killed both Ansel and Steward at 76.43 seconds, before Spot could activate. Spot later healed only himself.

I’m revising the structure to use two physicians and keep the lower duelist deployed. A second vanguard will fund that arrangement and add central damage; the next run will test its healing coverage and late blocking capacity.

revised_stage_understanding.simultaneous_demands: Rows1,3,4,6 each need interception or sufficient lethal contact; central two-row support must coexist with outer officers, sustained anti-air arts and medical recovery. Two civilians remain neutral and require roadblock clearance plus absence of officer/artillery threats.

candidates.assessment: Fang and Vanilla finance four melee lanes and improve central damage. Persistent lower duelist requires medical geometry that competes with aircraft and upper-outer recovery; two-block final armor queues remain unverified.

Sniper/caster shared lanes reduce ground slots, but straight crossing contact is short against3500HP runners and3300HP officers. Unsupported splash and probabilistic talents cannot provide missing kills.

Cheap three-block opening permits four simultaneous lanes. Living duelist release funds a durable lower replacement; Spot heals Ansel during first barrage, freeing Ansel for Steward. Later upper/lower armor damage is geometrically separated.

history_access_log.decision_support: Earlier single-physician caster/medic shared-splash deaths show need for actual early Spot healing; no historical loss time is a current deadline.

Read fixed-model cost/refund, range responsibilities and opening BLOCK/device events. The eight-ID WIN is evidence of mechanisms only. New seven-ID healing handoff, projectile locks and downstream outcomes require current simulation.

current_evidence.prediction_comparison: Predicted Spot-to-Ansel HEAL absent; observed Spot self-heals2422/2461 after medic death.

revised_tactical_requirements.primary_repair: Replace delayed local support with continuous second physician; test actual healing and two-slot central capacity.

Lower physician covers the duelist and stands outside caster-centered splash; after aircraft closure the caster returns to cover both central armored queues.

item.text:
Candidate 2 also completed as a LOSS. Hibiscus did heal Melantha as predicted, but her tile became the artillery impact point and splash hit four operators. She died at 71.43 seconds.

The next revision places Hibiscus away from that impact cluster and uses Spot as the initial lower-lane defender. This also changes the passage plan: the lower eastern roadblock will need later clearance, so civilian survival there must be tested explicitly.

revised_stage_understanding.simultaneous_demands: Rows1,3,4,6 each need interception or sufficient lethal contact; central two-row support must coexist with outer officers, sustained anti-air arts and medical recovery. Two civilians remain neutral and require roadblock clearance plus absence of officer/artillery threats.

candidates.assessment: Fang and Vanilla finance four melee lanes and improve central damage. Persistent lower duelist requires medical geometry that competes with aircraft and upper-outer recovery; two-block final armor queues remain unverified.

Sniper/caster shared lanes reduce ground slots, but straight crossing contact is short against3500HP runners and3300HP officers. Unsupported splash and probabilistic talents cannot provide missing kills.

Cheap three-block opening permits four simultaneous lanes. Living duelist release funds a durable lower replacement; Spot heals Ansel during first barrage, freeing Ansel for Steward. Later upper/lower armor damage is geometrically separated.

history_access_log.decision_support: Earlier single-physician caster/medic shared-splash deaths show need for actual early Spot healing; no historical loss time is a current deadline.

Read fixed-model cost/refund, range responsibilities and opening BLOCK/device events. The eight-ID WIN is evidence of mechanisms only. New seven-ID healing handoff, projectile locks and downstream outcomes require current simulation.

current_evidence.earliest_break: Hibiscus[5,5] receives1993 lower-duelist splash and becomes next shell center2143, damaging Vanilla, Melantha, Ansel and herself; she dies2143.
current_evidence.prediction_comparison: Hibiscus-to-Melantha heals1950/2036/2122 verified, but did not establish survival; subsequent caster deaths2593 followed missing second medical stream.

revised_tactical_requirements.win: Simulator WIN; selected/all-DEPLOY union<=7; zero leaks; both protected targets alive and reached; exhausted spawns and no active enemy.
revised_tactical_requirements.mechanics: Use supplied ordinary catalog and unchanged full execution facts including debug_configuration. No fake execution, repair, unsupported dodge, probabilistic extra-heal or death refunds.
revised_tactical_requirements.primary_repair: Remove artillery impact cluster and charge local defender early; verify both restrained civilians and final armored queue capacity.

revised_strategic_hypotheses.summary: Initial durable lower blocker and two separated physicians replace the fragile duelist/splash cluster. Four lanes remain occupied while caster kills aircraft and later clears both central armored queues. All three unbroken civilian devices receive explicit late clearance actions.

revision_hypothesis.tactical_hypothesis: Initial durable lower blocker and two separated physicians replace the fragile duelist/splash cluster. Four lanes remain occupied while caster kills aircraft and later clears both central armored queues. All three unbroken civilian devices receive explicit late clearance actions.
changed_responsibilities: Spot becomes the initial lower blocker; his early charge allows local healing during the first barrage.
Hibiscus moves away from the observed four-operator impact cluster and supplies the central/caster recovery stream.
Midnight and Steward own all later armor and device output; no withdrawn duelist contribution is assumed.
revision_hypothesis.if_expected_event_absent: Query actual caster/medic healing and shell recipients first. If survival succeeds, inspect restrained civilian and central armor pressure as independent downstream obligations.

explicit_assumptions: Historical device clearance and attack contacts are predictions, not current verified deadlines.
All timing is fixed at30FPS. No conditional action rescheduling occurs.
Death releases block and refunds zero; a dead operator cannot support later actions.

Three-block lower central capacity.
Upper outer block and eastern device clearance; available central ranged damage.
Initial durable lower outer blocker; roadblock beyond own-tile range remains until later caster clearance.
Heal both central blocks and caster; extend to Midnight.
Separate physician reaches Ansel, caster and both central blocks without lower-outer splash.
Sustain aircraft damage over complete eastern vertical passes.
After70s cooldown, arts coverage of both central rows3 and4.
Clear eastern lower roadblock at[6,6] and release surviving lower civilian.
Clear western upper roadblock at[1,2] and release upper civilian.
Clear western lower roadblock at[6,2] then allow final safe arrival before600s.

formation_structure.medical: Ansel[5,6]DOWN and Hibiscus[2,6]UP cover both central holders and caster[5,7]. Spot[6,5] supports Ansel, not caster directly. Hibiscus is outside lower-outer shell radius. Ansel extension covers Midnight.
formation_structure.artillery: Spot absorbs lower-directed shells under own active healing. No retreat changes the early target. Caster/Ansel share splash, but remote Hibiscus plus local Spot sustain actual patients. Existing projectiles persist.
formation_structure.roadblocks: Spot has only own-tile basic range and cannot clear eastern lower device. Lower civilian will remain restrained until caster's third deployment; survival during eastern aircraft passes is explicitly unverified. Upper Midnight clears eastern upper device. Final Midnight and fourth caster deployment clear both western devices.
formation_structure.late_pressure: No Melantha upper armor damage is credited. Midnight's actual free attacks and returning caster[2,5]UP must clear both central queues before overflow; range alone does not prove clearance.

item.text:
Candidate 3 survived the first barrage, but the uncleared lower roadblock kept a civilian inside the later artillery splash; both the civilian and Steward died at 131.43 seconds.

I’m testing a different firing position now. Steward will cover both central lanes continuously, and Midnight’s first arts skill will be reserved to help finish the aircraft. The physicians will cover separate areas from outside Steward’s splash radius. Melantha will again clear the lower eastern roadblock before the civilian arrives.

revised_stage_understanding.simultaneous_demands: Rows1,3,4,6 each need interception or sufficient lethal contact; central two-row support must coexist with outer officers, sustained anti-air arts and medical recovery. Two civilians remain neutral and require roadblock clearance plus absence of officer/artillery threats.

candidates.assessment: Fang and Vanilla finance four melee lanes and improve central damage. Persistent lower duelist requires medical geometry that competes with aircraft and upper-outer recovery; two-block final armor queues remain unverified.

Sniper/caster shared lanes reduce ground slots, but straight crossing contact is short against3500HP runners and3300HP officers. Unsupported splash and probabilistic talents cannot provide missing kills.

Cheap three-block opening permits four simultaneous lanes. Living duelist release funds a durable lower replacement; Spot heals Ansel during first barrage, freeing Ansel for Steward. Later upper/lower armor damage is geometrically separated.
New geometry trades eastern aircraft contact for continuous central armor output; held Midnight arts supplies western aircraft closure.

history_access_log.decision_support: Earlier single-physician caster/medic shared-splash deaths show need for actual early Spot healing; no historical loss time is a current deadline.

Read fixed-model cost/refund, range responsibilities and opening BLOCK/device events. The eight-ID WIN is evidence of mechanisms only. New seven-ID healing handoff, projectile locks and downstream outcomes require current simulation.

Candidate 4 failed on healing timing before the later damage plan could be tested fully. Hibiscus died between self-heals at 86.43 seconds. Delaying Midnight’s first skill also delayed the upper roadblock release, and that civilian died at 110.33 seconds.

For the final candidate, I’ll restore early arts damage to that roadblock and adjust the physicians’ deployment timing to change their heal cycles. Steward will keep continuous central coverage. Midnight’s proposed aircraft contribution was not observed, so I’m removing that assumption and treating aircraft closure as unresolved.
